transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… what finally made me call is I’ve been having these thoughts like, if I didn’t wake up tomorrow, maybe that would be easier. I don’t want to hurt myself, but it scared me enough to come in.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up tomorrow?

It’s been… not that long, I guess. Long enough that it scared me into making this appointment. I keep having that thought that if I just didn’t wake up, it might be easier. I don’t want to hurt myself, but… it’s been on my mind.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
Yeah… I think so. Most mornings lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, gray feeling, like everything’s already drained out before I even get dressed for work.
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do lately?
Not as much, no. I still get my paints out sometimes, or I’ll go to pottery class, but… I mostly just sit there looking at everything. It doesn’t feel the way it used to.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy as much as you used to?
Not really. I still set out my paints sometimes, or I think I’ll go to pottery, but once I’m there I just… stare at the materials. The spark isn’t really there like it used to be.
How many weeks have you been feeling this heavy, gray feeling?
Um… about six months, I guess. It’s been there long enough that things like my art class or morning walks don’t really seem to help much anymore.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?
I haven’t really been keeping track. My clothes seem about the same, I think… so no big change that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get things done lately?
Yeah… some days I’m kind of restless, pacing around the living room and picking at my cuticles. Other days, even just walking from the break room to the sales floor feels like I’m moving through mud.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I wouldn’t say I’ve really noticed it as a main thing.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling like you're moving through mud on some days?

I just mean… it’s like my body takes extra effort to get going. Like at work, walking from the break room to the sales floor feels oddly slow, heavier than it should. Other days it’s the opposite, I catch myself pacing at home or picking at my cuticles. It’s not constant.
Do you feel significantly worse in the mornings?
Yeah… mornings are usually worse. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like everything’s already kind of drained out before I even get dressed for work.
Are there any things that you used to enjoy doing, but now you don't find pleasure in them at all?

Yeah… painting, mostly. And pottery class. I still sort of make myself set the paints out, or I’ll go to class, but then I just sit there looking at everything. It doesn’t really… catch for me like it used to.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience any pleasure even when good things happen?

I guess… not unable with everything, but with the art stuff, yes. I’ll set out my paints or think I should go to pottery, and then I’m just sitting there staring at the materials. The spark I used to get from it just… isn’t there.
Do you usually feel restless and pace around, or is it more that you feel slowed down most of the time?

It’s kind of both, I guess. Some days I’m up pacing around the living room, picking at my cuticles… and other days I feel oddly slowed down, like even walking from the break room to the sales floor takes more effort than it should.
Do you usually feel more restless and agitated or slowed down most of the time?

It goes back and forth. Some days I’m restless, pacing around the living room and picking at my cuticles. Other days I feel slowed down… like even walking from the break room to the sales floor feels strangely slow.
Do you think the restless days happen more often than the slowed-down days?
I’m not sure which is more often, honestly. I just notice both… some days I’m pacing and picking at my cuticles, and other days I feel really slowed down, even just walking at work.
Do you feel like your heavy, gray feeling is at its worst every morning?
Most mornings, yes. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling… like everything’s already kind of drained out before I even get dressed for work.
Are your symptoms usually present for most of the day?
Most mornings, yes… that heavy, gray feeling is there when I wake up, like the color’s already drained out before I’m even dressed for the store. It tends to hang around for a lot of the day.
Have your symptoms been present for at least two weeks?

Yes… definitely more than two weeks. It’s been more like… around six months, this low, flat feeling. Long enough that things I used to do, like art class or morning walks, don’t really help much anymore.
Do you feel like your feelings of sadness or depression are worse in the morning and improve as the day goes on?
Yes… it’s usually worst when I first wake up. That heavy, gray feeling is just there before I even get ready for the store. It can ease a little later, I guess, but mornings are the hardest.
